title: A binuclear nickel(II) coordination compound bridged by thiazole-carboxylate ligand: Synthesis, structure and properties
abstract: The reaction of NiSO4-5H2O and 2-(2-aminothiazole-4-yl)-2-hydroxyiminoacetic acid (Haha) with NaOH in water afforded a Ni(II) coordination compound with formula Ni2(aha)4(H2O)2-3H2O (1). Compound 1 featured a binuclear structure, where the aha- tridentate ligands adopt the carboxylate, oxime, and thiazole groups to bridge with both Ni centers in a monodentate manner, respectively, with the aha- ligands terminating the Ni centers in chelating mode. In addition, compound 1 exhibited a band of 478 nm, falling in the orange region in CIE color coordinates, which is originating from ligand-centered emission. It is a second-harmonic generation (SHG) active with the SHG efficiency of 1.5 times as much as that of KH2PO4.. KEYWORDS :Coordination compound, Nickel, Fluorescence, Second-harmonic generation.
